solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Priests and doctors carry identification on top of uniform

indicators.note: the doctors hold the next pieces inside them, as if carrying them

parts.note: DRS is the plural abbreviation of doctor

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece 'on' another follows it, so the identification comes after
the top of a word is its first letter, so just the opening letter of uniform is used

explanation.surface: Clergy and medics carrying ID badges pinned to their uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the U comes before the ID inside the doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids were the priestly caste of the ancient Celts.

clue.text: Spanish ghost is expected to carry death

indicators.note: the word for expected carries the next piece inside it

parts.note: something due is expected
the end is death

explanation.surface: A Spanish spirit is supposed to bring death with it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish folklore a duende is a goblin or spirit, hence a ghost.

clue.text: What was left in duodenum after operation was not shaped

indicators.note: the letters are operated on, cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: What was left in the gut after surgery had lost its form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What was' at the start and 'was' before the definition are only padding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmoulded has not been formed in a mould, so it has no set form.

clue.text: Plays with Dutch and the French

parts.note: taken as it stands
les is French for 'the' before a plural

explanation.surface: Someone toys with the Dutch and the French in diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dandle is to bounce a child playfully on the knee, to play with it.

clue.text: Sheltered nameless canon in hut

indicators.note: the trimmed canon sits inside the hut

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so nameless means drop an N

parts.note: a musical canon is a round, where voices enter one after another with the same tune

explanation.surface: A cleric who has lost his name is sheltering in a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a clergyman, but it is the musical form where voices repeat a tune in turn; 'nameless' strips its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shrouded is covered and hidden, that is, sheltered from view.

clue.text: In financial difficulty Hare's down having

indicators.note: the only word left to signal the loss of an E from each piece; the clue gives no plainer deletion signal

parts.note: the animal's name is taken as it stands, the possessive adding nothing
feeling down is being depressed, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A financially stretched hare is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed has no clear signal for dropping an E from HARE and one from DEPRESSED; the blog jokes they 'lost two euros'. 'Having' is all that is left to carry it, so this clue is unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard-pressed means being under heavy pressure, often short of money.

clue.text: Strange chaps with time for a fag end

parts.note: odd means strange
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Odd men taking time over the last of a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a fag is a cigarette, and the fag end is its stub; figuratively, a leftover remnant.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover scrap or remnant, just as a fag end is the last useless bit.

clue.text: Edwin never finished: daughter's cross

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen

explanation.surface: Edwin left something unfinished, and his daughter is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mystery of Edwin Drood was the novel Dickens left incomplete at his death.

clue.text: Performed variable line with two fingers

parts.note: 'did act' means performed
Y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: Someone acted out a changeable line using two fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactyl means having two digits, from the Greek for two fingers.

clue.text: Thackeray's Henry has little time finally

indicators.note: the end has the next pieces held within it

parts.note: at the end means finally, so the word end stands in for it
S is the abbreviation for small, here clued by little
a mo is a moment, a short spell of time

explanation.surface: A Thackeray character, Henry, has little time left at last.
explanation.walkthrough: SMO goes inside END. Thackeray wrote the novel The History of Henry Esmond.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Esmond is the title hero of a Thackeray historical novel.

clue.text: Dictionary found in Yorkshire city

definitions.meaning: ... Crossword Solver's Dictionary is a well-known reference for solvers
a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: A dictionary turned up in a northern English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Bradford compiled a famous crossword dictionary, and the Yorkshire city shares the name.

clue.text: Twice swim in deep depression

parts.note: something done twice is doubled
a dip is a quick swim

explanation.surface: Swimming twice while feeling really low.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-dip recession is an economic slump that falls back into decline after a brief recovery.

clue.text: Elias feuded to become free from class-conscious social system

indicators.note: the two words change into another word made from their letters

explanation.surface: Elias quarrelled so as to escape a rigid class hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism was a rigid hierarchy of lords and vassals; to defeudalise is to free a society from it.

clue.text: Found in antiquated dictionary of mythological books

indicators.note: the letters are found sitting inside the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: Something found in an old dictionary about mythological books.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are the Old Norse collections of myth and poetry; eddic means relating to them.

clue.text: In ill-disposed manner fifty lads cede being converted

indicators.note: the three words are converted into a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Fifty young men grudgingly give way while being converted to a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Disaffected means discontented and hostile, so acting that way is behaving in an ill-disposed manner.

clue.text: Pedant son embraced by wood-nymph is in Utah

indicators.note: the nymph holds the son within her

parts.note: a dryad is a nymph of the woods in Greek myth

indicators.note: the short form sits inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah
's is the short form of is

explanation.surface: A dull scholar's son is in the arms of a wood-nymph out in Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Dryasdust, a Walter Scott invention, became a byword for a dull, pedantic scholar.

clue.text: Under-21 settled

parts.note: sub is Latin for under, as in subway
the number points to the clue at 21 across, whose answer means agreed

explanation.surface: A youth team, the under-21s, has settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under-21' looks like an age group, but it splits into 'Under' and a cross-reference to 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has subsided has sunk down and settled, like ground or floodwater.

clue.text: Openly issued gin: duly chastised

indicators.note: the words are punished and beaten into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone openly handed out gin and was rightly scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no disguise means doing it in the open, plainly and frankly.

clue.text: Persuaded French aristocrat to provoke rainfall all around

indicators.note: the seeding word goes all the way round the aristocrat

parts.note: clouds are seeded with particles to make rain fall
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A French nobleman was talked into making it rain everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to lead astray by persuasion or enticement.

clue.text: Terrified father holding on to Edmund

indicators.note: the father holds the next piece inside

parts.note: dad is father
re means on, concerning
Ed is short for Edmund

explanation.surface: A frightened father clings on to his son Edmund.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreaded can mean feared, frightened, though usually of the thing feared, as terrified is of the person.

clue.text: Bank said to be good place for diving

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the deep end of a swimming pool is where you can dive safely

explanation.surface: A riverbank is said to be a good diving spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun, a riverside, but it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to rely or count on them, just as one can bank on them.

clue.text: Agreed to get fish in South Dakota

indicators.note: the fish goes inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for the US state of South Dakota
the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to go fishing in South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: To side with someone is to agree with or support them.

clue.text: Avoid car

explanation.surface: Keep clear of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to avoid, and Dodge is a US car brand.

clue.text: Recipient of a garment drowned in river

indicators.note: the garment is sunk inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: Someone receives a piece of clothing that has been drowned in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is one of crossword-land's favourite rivers; the garment goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person a letter or parcel is sent to, its intended receiver.

clue.text: Did airman twitch when intended to teach?

parts.note: taken as it stands
AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A question about whether a flyer's nervous twitch was meant as a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic writing or speech is designed to instruct or give moral lessons.

clue.text: Quote notice to leader

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: An instruction to cite a notice to the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite or put forward as evidence, as one does in quoting.

clue.text: Extreme transaction about soft colour

indicators.note: the deed goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a deed is a legal document recording a transaction
P stands for piano, soft in music
to dye is to colour

explanation.surface: An extreme deal concerning a soft shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour is the verb form, to dye, not the past tense; the transaction's final letter closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deep-dyed is thoroughgoing and inveterate, an utter or extreme case.

clue.text: Red acted in one and made final version

definitions.meaning: joining the two words gives a single word meaning censored or prepared for publication
producing the final form of a text by revising it

explanation.surface: A communist performed in one play and produced the definitive version.
explanation.definitionFit: Redacting a document and preparing its final text are both what an editor does.
